habitat: Pairs live in the lower stratum of riverine and coastal thickets.
summary: An uncommon resident. The female has an all-black breast. The male has only a narrow black breast-band, on white underparts. Both have a red eye-wattle. The immature male lacks the breast-band. The call is a guttural chak-chak. The song is a weak tinkling er-er-fea-er-er-fee-fea, and there is a louder tree-tree-tree, che-chreet-che-chreet-che-chreet. Newman’s size line is printed as an error, so no length is stored. The Kemp paper name Wattleeyed Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Chinspot Batis has a yellow eye and no red eye-wattle. Its female has a rufous chin-spot, not an all-black breast.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The size line on Newman’s page is printed as #VALUE!, so size is omitted rather than guessed. The immature male is only the missing breast-band. Bill, iris, legs, wings and the back were not given colours. The red mark is the eye-wattle. No back or flight photograph was found. The only grade A recording is a duet and song from Zambia. No separate chak-chak call was selected. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Wattleeyed Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.
